title: Design a UPI payments experience for elderly users
prompt: Design a UPI payments experience for people over 65 in India. How would you approach it?
brief: Users: 65+, varying digital literacy, often dependent on children for tech help, fear of fraud, vision/motor limitations, regional language preference. Good answers: pick a segment (e.g., semi-urban retirees with smartphones who currently use cash), map the journey and pain points (onboarding, trust, error recovery, fraud), prioritise (e.g., fraud anxiety + confirmation clarity), propose features (trusted-contact approval for large payments, voice confirmation in local language, large-type mode, pay-to-known-contacts-only mode), define metrics (weekly active elderly payers, successful transaction rate, fraud-report rate as guardrail).
strong_answer_notes: Explicit segmentation and prioritisation; trade-off between safety and friction; north-star plus guardrail metrics.

title: Order volume dropped 8% week-on-week
prompt: You're the PM for a food delivery app. Orders dropped 8% week-on-week in one city. How would you figure out what happened?
brief: Hidden cause: an app release 6 days ago changed the default address logic; users with multiple saved addresses see a 'service unavailable' error when their default is set to an office address on weekends. Orders from users with 2+ saved addresses fell 25%; others are flat. Clarifications: no outages, no competitor promotions, no weather events, restaurants on the platform flat. Good answers: check data validity, internal vs external factors, segment by platform/app version/user type/geography, find the release, propose a fix and a rollback plan.
strong_answer_notes: Systematic segmentation; checks recent releases early; separates internal and external causes; proposes a fix plus monitoring.

title: Should a video platform launch 'watch parties'?
prompt: You're a PM at a video streaming platform in India. Leadership is asking whether to build a 'watch party' feature where friends can watch together remotely. How would you decide?
brief: Context: 40% of sessions are on mobile; social sharing of clips is high; engagement is flat; building costs ~2 quarters of a 6-engineer team. Competitor launched watch parties with low reported usage. Good answers: define the goal (engagement? retention? acquisition?), target users (young users watching cricket/series with friends), test demand cheaply (fake door, clip-sharing data), size impact, weigh opportunity cost, define success metrics and a minimal version (e.g., for live cricket only).
strong_answer_notes: Goal-first thinking; cheap validation; opportunity cost; MVP scoping.

title: Success metrics for a 'reorder' button
prompt: A quick-commerce app is launching a one-tap 'reorder your last basket' button. What metrics would you use to measure its success?
brief: Goal: faster repeat purchases and higher order frequency. Good answers: north-star (orders per active user per week) plus feature metrics (adoption: % of orders via reorder; time to checkout), quality/guardrails (basket edits after reorder, cancellations, AOV change, item substitution complaints), and a controlled experiment design.
strong_answer_notes: Ties metrics to goal; includes guardrails; proposes an A/B test.
